title: COP31 leaders' summit opens; PM meets Uzbek president in Antalya
excerpt: Guterres warned the climate crisis is outrunning the world. Bangladesh's grant-based adaptation ask still has no figure in the talks.

image.alt: Delegates seated around the negotiating tables at the COP31 Presidency's energy ministerial meeting in Antalya, Türkiye, on 10 November 2026
image.credit: Necati Savas / European Union, 2026, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0

content:
The two-day Antalya Leaders' Summit opened at COP31 in Türkiye on Wednesday, 11 November, with UN Secretary-General António Guterres warning that "the climate crisis is outrunning us". Prime Minister Tarique Rahman joined the opening session at about 12:15pm local time (3:15pm Dhaka) and later held talks with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, bdnews24.com and The Daily Star reported.

What Guterres and Erdoğan said

Guterres told leaders that "fossil fuels must go the way of the dinosaurs, but that won't happen on its own", adding that "the dinosaurs did not have a lobby, but fossil fuels do", Al Jazeera reported. He said the last four years were the hottest on record. The United States stayed away from the talks for a second year.

Host President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan pressed countries to sign up to Türkiye's zero-waste initiative, which targets methane, food waste and the circular economy. He said recycling in Türkiye rose from about 13% in 2017 to about 40% by the end of 2025, the Associated Press reported.

Bangladesh's day in Antalya

  • Uzbek talks: the meeting with Mirziyoyev began at 2:45pm local time and lasted about half an hour. The two leaders discussed bilateral relations, climate change impacts and wider cooperation, according to Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu. Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman and State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir attended. No agreement was announced.
  • China: a meeting with Chinese Vice-President Han Zheng was on the schedule. By 9:30pm Dhaka time, no Bangladeshi or Chinese account of it had been published.
  • Leaders' Lounge: before the session the prime minister had brief informal talks with leaders including Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari, bdnews24.com reported.
  • Bangladesh Pavilion: at 4:50pm local time he toured the pavilion, which shows jute products, tree planting and adaptation work. Environment Minister Abdul Awal Mintoo, State Minister Shaikh Faridul Islam and Special Assistant Saimum Parvez received him, The Business Standard reported.

All details of the prime minister's meetings come from the government's press wing. Neither side published quotes.

In the negotiating rooms

The leaders' speeches run alongside technical talks that began on 9 November. The agenda was adopted only after a dispute in which finance and trade split developed and developing countries, TFI Post reported. Developing countries, led by the African Group, want a number attached to the COP30 goal of tripling adaptation finance by 2035. Before the summit, EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra called fresh demands for new finance commitments "dead in the water", the same report said.

Why it matters

Bangladesh's main ask in Antalya is three times more adaptation finance, paid as grants. The opening day showed little sign of new money: the host is focused on waste and electrification, and the EU has said new pledges are unlikely. NGOs that depend on climate funds for coastal and flood-prone work should not plan on a bigger adaptation pot from this COP until a figure appears in a draft text.

What to watch

  • The prime minister's national statement to the plenary on Thursday, 12 November.
  • Any read-out of the Han Zheng meeting, given China's role in Bangladesh's infrastructure and Teesta plans.
  • Finance and trade day on 13 November, and the first draft decision text on adaptation finance.
